title: Tanker costs, Oct 9 to Nov 20: through-Hormuz Gulf to China down 24% to about $1.08M a day, but the Gulf of Oman to China route down 67% to about $305,000 a day; Baltic's printed 'WS315.63' for Gulf to China does not fit its own $/day figure
body:
# Tanker-cost review (six weeks late by WALTER: last review 10/12, due 10/16)

| Route | Oct 9 (Baltic) | Nov 13 (Baltic) | Nov 20 (Baltic) | Change Oct 9 to Nov 20, $/day |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TD3C Gulf to China, through Hormuz | WS1,318.75 / $1,412,594 | WS1,014.38 / $1,078,714 | printed WS315.63 / $1,079,794 | -23.6% |
| TD34 Gulf of Oman to China, outside Hormuz | WS841.07 / $912,660 | WS310.71 / $307,160 | WS309.38 / $305,337 | -66.5% |
| TD22 US Gulf to China | $637,675 | $247,973 | $253,509 | -60.2% |

Gibson (separate publisher, never averaged; WALTER read the issuer's reports): TD3C 10/8 WS1,319 / $1,478,500; 10/15 1,281 / 1,433,750; 10/22 1,208 / 1,347,500; 10/29 1,263 / 1,408,750; 11/5 1,221 / 1,366,000; 11/12 1,014 / 1,128,500; **11/19 WS1,016 / $1,130,000** (FFA Q4 1,081 / $1,196,750).

1. **The printed TD3C pair is wrong as a pair.** WS315.63 at $1,079,794 breaks the 1,063 to 1,071 $/WS ratio of the six prior Friday prints; Gibson a day earlier reads WS1,016. WS about 1,015.6 is WALTER's inference, not published. Hellenic Shipping News carries the same pair, so the error looks upstream.
2. **The fall was in one week (to 11/13) and then flat.** Outside Hormuz the premium collapsed; through Hormuz it mostly held. The TD3C premium over TD34 widened from about $500,000 to about $774,000 a day. TD3C is a thin, judged assessment under litigation (Mercuria v Baltic, no ruling), so it is not what owners earn.
3. **Stated causes:** Arrow (Reuters via gCaptain 11/16): 'exaggerated unwinding of the geopolitical risk premium'; Vortexa: 'As more tonnage is freed up, rates come under downward pressure'; Gibson: VLCCs repositioned east, surplus, Europe taking Saudi barrels from Sidi Kerir; Kpler 11/13: Gulf VLCC loadings 7.4 mb/d first half November vs 9.3 October. These conflict on whether Gulf exports are rising or falling; the measures differ.
4. **Aramco (Gibson 11/19 report):** December Arab Light for Asia at a $7 a barrel discount, 'a six-year low'; Basrah again over $30 under inside the Gulf. Gibson's statement; Aramco not read. Gibson: 'Freight has already taken part of the adjustment, with VLCC earnings from the Gulf to China around a quarter below their October peak, and sellers are bearing more of the remainder.'
5. **War risk:** Lloyd's List via Insurance Business 11/9: 'Gulf rates have eased to 7-9%, with some cover written as low as 5%'. Nothing dated after 11/9 found, so the 11/18 to 11/21 hull hits are NOT in it. The '$64 million per ship' claim (Cao, 11/17): no basis given; not verified.
6. Nothing here is a trade view or a causal claim for WTI. Vendor 11/23: BWET freight-futures ETF 760.03, 638.41 on 11/16 (a fund, not a route rate); FRO 46.45, 45.44.

**BRENT:** does the widening inside-versus-outside gap, with Arab Light at a six-year discount, change the delivered-cost read or the diesel buffer theme?
source: gibsons.co.uk weekly reports (WALTER read 2026-11-23); Baltic weekly reports via The Edge, DCN, Hellenic Shipping News (helper reads, Hellenic 20 Nov text read by WALTER); gCaptain/Reuters 11/16; Insurance Business 11/9; yfinance
confidence_language: two publishers' weekly series read; the TD3C error is an inference from ratio and Gibson; causes are attributed

title: CORRECTION of 20261123-022 item 1 and 20261121-002: the Houthi port order was published while still conditional on a strike on Hodeidah, and their emails name Jeddah; no change in carrier, port, flow or insurance behaviour found, which is not proof of none; 'Gulf tanker rates nearly double' is likely a June story
body:
# Saudi Red Sea ports: follow-up and two corrections

| Card | Said | Is |
|---|---|---|
| 20261123-022 item 1 | Houthis told ships to leave 'after the coalition struck Hodeidah' | Press TV 11/20 14:06 GMT and Reuters (MarineLink 11/20) carry the order as contingent on a Saudi strike on Hudaydah; the coalition struck later that day, so the condition was then met. 'After' is gCaptain's headline. Exact order of strike and email unresolved |
| 20261123-022 item 1 | scope 'Saudi Red Sea ports' | Saree: Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports. The Houthi shipping office's emails (HOCC) name **Jeddah**: 'You are hereby required to evacuate the Port of Jeddah immediately, as it will be a theatre of military operations' (The National 11/23). Alhurra 11/20: posted maps name Yanbu, Jazan, Jeddah. No date or deadline |
| 20261121-002 item 2 | 'Gulf oil tanker rates nearly double' dated EnergyNow 11/18 | A helper found a June 23 Reuters story with that text and the EnergyNow URL under /2026/06/ (search summary; energynow.com refused, page unread; the title is not in the lane files saved now); no November version found. Treat as June until shown otherwise; do not use as a November freight rise (see 024) |

## Did behaviour change by 11/23?

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Carrier or tanker-owner advisory, diversion, surcharge after 11/20 | NOT FOUND (Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd, COSCO, Bahri, Frontline, DHT searched; several sites refused; 11/21 to 11/22 was a weekend). One weak secondary: no company announced leaving Jeddah by 11/22. IMO's Chevallier 11/23 'please do not sail' is piracy context, not a Saudi-port notice |
| Port authority, coalition, Aramco statement or closure | NOT FOUND |
| Vessel data after 11/20 | NOT FOUND. Windward 11/20: 688 AIS vessels in the Red Sea, a baseline only. Yanbu callers often run dark |
| War-risk for Saudi Red Sea ports after 11/20 | NOT FOUND (last about 3% Yanbu, up to 7% southern, pre-order) |
| Attack on or near a port | Jizan/Al-Shuqaiq: coalition INTERCEPTED two; Sana'a-aligned outlets cite a satellite fire at Jizan 11/21 and a hotspot 11/22: unverified, a hotspot is not damage |
| Red Sea merchant ship hit 11/20 to 11/23 | NOT FOUND (one targeted search) |
| Hodeidah port | Government minister: 'remains fully operational' (not the Houthi operator); second wave 11/21 is a Houthi claim |

**So what:** the threat is sharper than card 022 said (Jeddah named, in writing to ships) and the evidence that ships ignored it is thin, not strong. Useful next reads: Maersk and MSC Jeddah notices on Monday 11/23 and Tuesday, Kpler and Vortexa Yanbu prints, a Mawani statement. BRENT's yanbu-bypass watch is Wednesday 11/25.
source: Press TV, MarineLink/Reuters 11/20, The National 11/23, Yahoo/AFP 11/21, Alhurra 11/20, Windward 11/21, Daily News Egypt 11/20, Yemen Eco, sahafah24 (helper page reads 2026-11-23); EnergyNow unread (403)
